nodes.summary: For every natural number $k \ge 2$, the numbers $11(10^k - 1)$ and $22(10^k - 1)$ both have exactly $k + 2$ decimal digits, the decimal reversal of $11(10^k - 1)$ equals $9 \cdot 11(10^k - 1)$, and the decimal reversal of $22(10^k - 1)$ equals $4 \cdot 22(10^k - 1)$.
nodes.title: Basic reverse divisors

nodes.summary: Let $B \ge 2$ be a natural number and let $n$ be a natural number dividing $B^2 - 1$. Then $n$ divides the base-$B$ reversal of every multiple of $n$.
nodes.title: In base $B$, divisors of $B^2 - 1$ divide reversals of their multiples

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a reverse divisor with $L$ decimal digits, where $L \le 7$. Then $n = 11(10^{L-2} - 1)$ or $n = 22(10^{L-2} - 1)$, where $L - 2$ is read as $0$ when $L < 2$.
nodes.title: Reverse divisors with at most seven digits

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number such that $\gcd(n, 10) = 1$, or $n$ equals its decimal reversal, or $n$ is a reverse divisor. Then there is a natural number $k_0 \ge 1$ such that $n$ divides the decimal reversal of $k_0 n$.
nodes.title: Sufficient conditions for a multiple with divisible reversal

nodes.summary: Every reverse divisor has at least four decimal digits.
nodes.title: Reverse divisors have at least four digits

nodes.summary: The positive integers with property $P^*$ are the divisors of $99$. A natural number $n \ge 1$ has property $P^*$ if and only if $n$ divides $99$.
nodes.title: The positive integers with property $P^*$ are the divisors of $99$

nodes.summary: Unfolding property $P^*$. A natural number $n$ has property $P^*$ if and only if $n$ divides the decimal reversal of every multiple of $n$.
nodes.title: Unfolding property $P^*$

nodes.summary: Divisors of $99$ have property $P^*$. Every divisor of $99$ has property $P^*$.
nodes.title: Divisors of $99$ have property $P^*$

nodes.summary: Property $P^*$. A natural number $n$ has property $P^*$ if $n$ divides the decimal reversal of every multiple of $n$.
nodes.title: Property $P^*$

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number not divisible by $10$, and suppose that $n$ divides the decimal reversal of $k_0 n$ for some natural number $k_0 \ge 1$. Then there are infinitely many natural numbers $k \ge 1$ such that $n$ divides the decimal reversal of $k n$.
nodes.title: Infinitely many multiples with divisible reversal

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $g$, $k$ and $m$, the Young graph $Y(g, k)$ of the $k$-reverse multiples in base $g$ is complete on $m$ nodes: the nodes other than its distinguished starting node form the complete directed graph on $m$ nodes, so $Y(g, k)$ has $m + 1$ nodes in all; the node $[0, 0]$ is one of these $m$ nodes, and the starting node has an edge to every node except $[0, 0]$.
nodes.title: Complete Young graphs

nodes.summary: A natural number $n$ is a reverse divisor if and only if $n > 0$ and there is a natural number $k \ge 2$ such that the decimal reversal of $n$ equals $kn$.
nodes.title: Characterization of reverse divisors

nodes.summary: A natural number $n$ is a reverse divisor if $n > 0$ and there is a natural number $k \ge 2$ such that the decimal reversal of $n$ equals $kn$. Since $n > 0$, such a $k$ is unique; it is called the quotient of $n$.
nodes.title: Reverse divisor

nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a set, let $P$ be a predicate on $V$ and let $\prec$ be a binary relation on $V$. A node $v \in V$ is retained with respect to $P$ and $\prec$ if and only if $P(v)$ holds or there is a node $w \in V$ with $P(w)$ and $v \prec w$.
nodes.title: Characterization of retained nodes

nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a set, let $P$ be a predicate on $V$ (the pivot nodes) and let $\prec$ be a binary relation on $V$. A node $v \in V$ is retained with respect to $P$ and $\prec$ if $P(v)$ holds or there is a node $w \in V$ with $P(w)$ and $v \prec w$.
nodes.title: Retained node

nodes.summary: For every natural number $r$, let $a = (10^r - 1) \cdot 100 + 89$, the integer whose decimal digits are $r$ nines followed by $89$, and let $b = 10^{r+2} - 1$, the integer whose decimal digits are $r + 2$ nines. Then the remainder of $ab$ modulo $10^{r+2}$ is $11$; that is, the last $r + 2$ decimal digits of $ab$ are $r$ zeros followed by $11$.
nodes.title: A product congruent to $11$ modulo a power of ten

nodes.summary: For $k \ge 2$, the number $11 \cdot (10^k - 1)$ lacks property $P^*$. For every natural number $k \ge 2$, the number $11 \cdot (10^k - 1)$ does not have the property $P^*$.
nodes.title: For $k \ge 2$, the number $11 \cdot (10^k - 1)$ lacks property $P^*$

nodes.summary: No reverse divisor has property $P^*$. If $n$ is a reverse divisor, then $n$ does not have the property $P^*$.
nodes.title: No reverse divisor has property $P^*$

nodes.summary: Positive integers sharing a factor with $10$ lack property $P^*$. If $n \ge 1$ is a natural number with $\gcd(n, 10) \ne 1$, then $n$ does not have the property $P^*$.
nodes.title: Positive integers sharing a factor with $10$ lack property $P^*$

nodes.summary: Reverse divisors with quotient $4$ lack property $P^*$. If $n > 0$ is a natural number whose decimal reversal equals $4n$, then $n$ does not have the property $P^*$.
nodes.title: Reverse divisors with quotient $4$ lack property $P^*$

nodes.summary: Palindromes with property $P^*$. Let $n \ge 1$ be a natural number that is a decimal palindrome, that is, whose decimal reversal equals $n$. If $n$ has the property $P^*$, then $n$ is one of $1$, $3$, $9$, $11$, $33$ and $99$.
nodes.title: Palindromes with property $P^*$

nodes.summary: If $n$ is a reverse divisor, then the decimal reversal of $n$ equals $4n$ or $9n$.
nodes.title: Reverse divisors have quotient $4$ or $9$

nodes.summary: Let $g$, $k$ and $m$ be natural numbers with $2 \le k < g$ and $m \ge 2$. Then the Young graph $Y(g, k)$ is complete on $m$ nodes if and only if
nodes.title: Characterization of complete Young graphs

nodes.summary: Let $g$ and $k$ be integers with $2 \le k < g$, and let $N = (a_n a_{n-1} \cdots a_0)_g$ have base-$g$ digits $a_0, \dots, a_n \in \{0, \dots, g - 1\}$, with units digit $a_0$ and leading digit $a_n \ne 0$. Suppose $N$ is a $(g, k)$ reverse multiple, that is, $k N = (a_0 a_1 \cdots a_n)_g$, and that $a_0 + a_n = g$. Then $(k + 1) a_n = g$; in particular $k + 1$ divides $g$ and $a_n = g / (k + 1)$.
nodes.title: Sloane's endpoint formula for reverse multiples

nodes.summary: Let $g$ and $k$ be integers with $2 \le k < g$, and let $a$ and $b$ be base-$g$ digits, $0 \le a, b < g$, with $a \ne 0$, such that $(a\,b)_g$ is a $(g, k)$ reverse multiple, that is, $k (a g + b) = b g + a$. Then $a + b < g$, so $a + b$ is a base-$g$ digit, and $(a\,(a + b)\,b)_g$ is again a $(g, k)$ reverse multiple, that is, $k (a g^2 + (a + b) g + b) = b g^2 + (a + b) g + a$.
nodes.title: Sutcliffe's theorem on two- and three-digit reverse multiples

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a labeled directed graph, let $P$ be a predicate on its vertices, let $\prec$ be a binary relation on its vertices, and let $e$ be an edge of $G$ whose source and target are both retained with respect to $P$ and $\prec$, viewed as an edge of the Young graph of $G$ with respect to $P$ and $\prec$. The label of $e$ in the Young graph is its label in $G$.
nodes.title: Label of an edge in the Young graph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a labeled directed graph, let $P$ be a predicate on its vertices, let $\prec$ be a binary relation on its vertices, and let $e$ be an edge of $G$ whose source and target are both retained with respect to $P$ and $\prec$, viewed as an edge of the Young graph of $G$ with respect to $P$ and $\prec$. The source of $e$ in the Young graph, viewed as a vertex of $G$, is the source of $e$ in $G$.
nodes.title: Source of an edge in the Young graph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a labeled directed graph, let $P$ be a predicate on its vertices, let $\prec$ be a binary relation on its vertices, and let $e$ be an edge of $G$ whose source and target are both retained with respect to $P$ and $\prec$, viewed as an edge of the Young graph of $G$ with respect to $P$ and $\prec$. The target of $e$ in the Young graph, viewed as a vertex of $G$, is the target of $e$ in $G$.
nodes.title: Target of an edge in the Young graph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a labeled directed graph with vertex set $V$, edge set $E$ and label set $L$, let $P$ be a predicate on $V$ and let $\prec$ be a binary relation on $V$. The Young graph of $G$ with respect to $P$ and $\prec$ is the labeled directed graph with label set $L$ whose vertices are the vertices of $G$ that are retained with respect to $P$ and $\prec$, whose edges are the edges of $G$ whose source and target are…
nodes.title: Young graph of a labeled directed graph

nodes.summary: Let $g, k, n$ be natural numbers with $2 \le k < g$, and let $a_0, \dots, a_{n-1}$ be natural numbers with $a_i < g$ for every $i$. Then $k \sum_{i\lt n} a_i g^i = \sum_{i\lt n} a_{n-1-i} g^i$ if and only if there is a unique sequence of natural numbers $r_0, \dots, r_n$ with $r_0 = 0$, $r_n = 0$ and, for every $i < n$, $r_{i+1} < k$ and $k a_i + r_i = a_{n-1-i} + r_{i+1} g$.
nodes.title: Carry equations for reverse multiples, general form

Then $k \sum_{i\lt n} a_i g^i = \sum_{i\lt n} a_{n-1-i} g^i$, that is, $k$ times the number with base-$g$ digits $a_{n-1}, \dots, a_0$ (most significant first) equals the number with these digits reversed, if and only if there is a unique…
nodes.title: Carry equations for reverse multiples

nodes.summary: Let $g$ and $k$ be natural numbers with $2 \le k < g$. A $(g, k)$ reverse multiple is a list of base-$g$ digits $d_1, d_2, \dots, d_n$, most significant first, with $n \ge 2$, $d_1 \ne 0$, $d_n \ne 0$ and $d_i < g$ for every $i$, such that $k$ times the number $\sum_{i=1}^{n} d_i g^{n-i}$ equals the number $\sum_{i=1}^{n} d_{n+1-i} g^{n-i}$ whose digits are those of the first in reverse order. can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
